entities.summary:
István Várday was a Hungarian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation during the 15th century. Born in Szabolcs County, Hungary in 1420, Várdai rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming Bishop of Győr in 1458 and eventually Cardinal-Deacon of Santa Maria in Minerva in 1462.

 He was instrumental in the establishment of several monasteries and colleges, including the famous Esterházy College in Sopron, which became a center for humanist education. Várdai also contributed significantly to the translation of Latin texts into Hungarian, helping to preserve ancient knowledge during a time of significant cultural upheaval.

 Despite facing opposition from Protestant reformers, Várdai remained steadfast in his devotion to the Catholic Church, and his legacy as a champion of orthodoxy has endured for centuries. His contributions to education, literature, and the spread of Catholicism helped shape the intellectual and religious landscape of medieval Europe.
